Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead: - Group nodes by **category** — all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal. - For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** — warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert. - Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps). - Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp. - **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept — those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.) **Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** — title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds. **Light/dark mode quick pick** — use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values: - **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle** - **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle** - Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` — paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke="#..."` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink. For status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps. <!-- @generated by apps/cds-docs/scripts/gen-cds-skill.mjs from packages/cds/{CLAUDE.md,docs/**}. Do not edit by hand — edit the source docs and re-run `yarn workspace @ant/cds-docs gen:cds-skill`. --> # CDS tokens — vanilla The Claude Design System token vocabulary for plain HTML/CSS/SVG surfaces without React or Tailwind. Tokens are unprefixed CSS custom properties (`--text-primary`, `--surface-1`, `--border`) declared on `:root` by `@ant/cds/tokens.vanilla.css`, with dark-mode overrides under `[data-mode="dark"]` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. References below to `CdsRoot`, `Button`, or Tailwind utilities belong to the React build; in vanilla, read a utility like `bg-surface-1` as the underlying `var(--surface-1)`. ## Rules ### Token rule Reference purpose-layer tokens as CSS custom properties: ```css /* GOOD */ background: var(--surface-1); color: var(--text-secondary); border: 0.5px solid var(--border); /* BAD — raw hex, invisible in dark mode */ color: #3d3d3a; ``` | Property | Tokens | | ---------- | ------ | | Background | `--surface-{0..3,popover,panel}` · `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro,neutral}` · `--bg-tint-{hue}` · `--fill-{role}` | | Text | `--text-{primary,secondary,muted,disabled}` · `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro}` · `--text-tint-{hue}` · `--on-{role}` | | Border | `--border` (default hairline) · `--border-{strong,stronger}` · `--border-{role}` | | Sizing | `--h-control` · `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}` · `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` · `--radius` | | Typography | `--font-{sans,mono,voice}` · `--font-size-{caption,footnote,body,prose,code,heading,title}` | | Shadow | `--shadow-{sm,md,lg,popover}` | | Motion | `--dur-{fast,snap,base,slow}` · `--ease-{out,snap,overshoot}` | ### Dark mode rule Dark mode is `[data-mode="dark"]` on `:root` (or `prefers-color-scheme: dark` with no explicit `data-mode`). All tokens flip automatically — never hardcode a dark-mode override. ### Muted text rule Supporting copy uses `color: var(--text-secondary)`; reserve `var(--text-muted)` for placeholders, captions, and metadata. **Never** `opacity` on text — opacity multiplies against the background and drifts per-surface. ### Accent rule At most **one** accent-filled (`variant="primary"`) Button per view; siblings use `secondary` or `ghost`. The `brand` (clay) role is reserved for Claude-initiated actions — send, generate — never ordinary user CTAs. ### Restraint rule Default to the quieter, lighter option — "too cluttered" is the most common design note. - `secondary` is the default Button; `primary` / `brand` read as aggressive — don't reach for them in popovers, banners, or dense tool/canvas surfaces. - Avoid disabled buttons. Keep them enabled and respond on use (disabled controls are low-contrast and show no tooltip on touch); use `disabledReason` only when you genuinely must disable. - Dense lists: bordered rows, not rounded-rect cards. ### Elevation rule `surface-0` is the page canvas (via `--page-bg`; set it with `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop); `1`/`2`/`3` step above it. Overlay popups and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` (and the `useCdsSurface()` context) to the plane they paint, so knockout effects inside them blend into the elevated surface — don't hand-roll `--page-bg` overrides on floating chrome, and don't author new styles against `var(--page-bg)` inside overlays (use `shadow-focus`/`bg-page` or `useCdsSurface()` — the var is an implementation detail slated to move to a dedicated ambient var). At most **two** floating elevations (`panel` / `popover`) on screen at once. A third floating layer means `Dialog`, not popover-on-popover. Flat in-flow tiles (`rounded-card bg-surface-1 shadow-card-ring`) have no depth and don't count toward this limit. --- ## CDS principles How something feels like Claude — the philosophy behind the tokens. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_. ## Claude-native cds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. The `CLAUDE.md` you're reading is the system prompt; component docs are structured for retrieval; utilities are named so a model can guess them; the GenerateDemo page proves the loop works. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too. ## Clay is Claude's color `brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does — send, generate, the spark mark. User-driven primary actions take the neutral `accent` blue; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper. ## Serif is Claude's voice Claude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces. ## Density adapts to the surface Console, claude.ai and antfarm share the same components — `compact` for dev tools and power users, `comfortable` for consumer apps. Density is one switch on `CdsRoot`, not a per-component prop, so a product can change its feel without forking a single component. ## Built to be composed, not overridden Every component takes `className` for placement and behavior, every token is a public CSS var, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) sit under the porcelain helpers so you can recombine them. The system expects you to compose _with_ it — wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots, build new things from its tokens — not restyle it from outside or fork it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the system is missing something: the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it. ## Restraint over options One accent per view, one elevation step, t-shirt sizes instead of 0–12 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart — consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them. ## CDS tokens Every visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `yarn gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code. ## The layer model ``` 1. Base palette --{hue}-{stop} literal hex, mode-stable (gray, red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, violet, magenta) 2. Theme ramps --neutral-N gray-N in light, gray-(900-N) in dark --alpha-N neutral-900 @ fixed opacity (so it flips too) 3. Elevation --surface-{0..3} 0 = darkest, 3 = lightest, in BOTH modes 4. Purpose --surface-{popover, what components actually consume; includes the panel}, --text-*, role mappings ({fill|bg|border|text}-{role}) --fill-*, --on-* — page-bg --page-bg hook the host app sets to its canvas color 5. Density --h-control*, rem lengths (px ÷ 16); remapped by --pad-*, --gap-*, [data-density] --radius, --font-size-*, --leading-* 6. Motion --dur-*, durations + easing curves (mode/density-invariant) --ease-* ``` **Components only read layer 4 (and 5 for sizing).** Layers 1–3 are wiring. --- ## 1. Base palette Literal hex values, mode-stable — `gray-500` is the same pixel in light and dark. The ramp variables resolve anywhere in the document, not only under a `.cds-root`. Nine hues share one 36-stop grid (0, 10–100 by 10, 150–800 by 50, 810–900 by 10); every hue anchors 0 = `#ffffff` and 900 = `#0b0b0b`. Rarely referenced directly — reach for layers 2–4 and let them resolve here. --- ## 2. Theme ramps `--neutral-N` is `gray-N` in light and `gray-(900-N)` in dark, so `neutral-0` is always the near-background end and `neutral-900` the near-foreground end. Use it for "contrast against the page" (text, borders, fills); use `gray-*` when you mean a specific pixel value regardless of mode. `--alpha-N` is `neutral-900` at fixed opacity — a black wash in light, a white wash in dark, without per-mode overrides. --- ## 3. Elevation | Token | Light | Dark | Use case | | ----------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------ | | `--surface-0` | `gray-20` | `gray-900` | Page | | `--surface-1` | `gray-10` | `gray-850` | In-flow card | | `--surface-2` | `gray-0` | `gray-830` | Panel | | `--surface-3` | `gray-0` | `gray-800` | Popover | The ordinal is absolute lightness in both modes: 0 is the darkest, 3 the lightest. `--surface-panel` and `--surface-popover` alias levels 2 and 3. The page canvas is the app's own choice — set it via `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop (which emits `--page-bg`) so knockout hairlines (focus ring inset, Pulse halo) blend into it; it defaults to `surface-0`. Inside elevated chrome the blend target is not the page: overlay popups (`Dialog`, `Menu`, `Popover`, `Combobox`, `Toast`, `CoachMark`) and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` to the surface they actually paint (`surface-3` for popover chrome, `surface-2` for panels) and provide the same value to JS consumers through the surface context — `useCdsSurface()`, below. --- ## 4. Purpose **This is the layer components consume.** ### Roles Each role maps a semantic meaning to a hue. Property-first pattern: `--fill-{role}` (solid hue-450), `--fill-{role}-hover` (hue-400), `--bg-{role}` (hue-100 / dark hue-800), `--border-{role}` (solid hue-250 in light / hue-700 in dark), `--text-{role}` (600 fg). Warning's fill diverges: yellow-200 / hover yellow-250. Brand uses named `clay-emphasized` / hover `clay` (not hue stops). The five hue-backed roles reach their hue through internal aliases (`--role-{role}-{stop}`, plus `--role-{role}-fill`, `--role-{role}-fill-hover` and `--role-{role}-on`): CSS-only wiring, not part of the token vocabulary, so never reference them. Charts, palette tints and the `{hue}-{stop}` utilities read the hue ramps directly. | Role | Hue | Tokens | | --------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `accent` | blue | `--fill-accent{,-hover}`, `--bg-accent`, `--bg-accent-muted`, `--border-accent`, `--text-accent` | | `brand` | clay | `--fill-brand{,-hover}`, `--on-brand` (fill-only — no text/bg/border) | | `danger` | red | `--fill-danger{,-hover}`, `--bg-danger`, `--border-danger`, `--text-danger` | | `success` | green | `--fill-success{,-hover}`, `--bg-success`, `--border-success`, `--text-success` | | `warning` | yellow | `--fill-warning{,-hover}`, `--bg-warning`, `--border-warning`, `--text-warning` | | `pro` | purple | `--fill-pro{,-hover}`, `--bg-pro`, `--border-pro`, `--text-pro` | `accent` additionally carries `--bg-accent-muted` (a 10% `fill-accent` wash over transparent, `color-mix` in srgb): an accent wash one weight below `bg-accent`, for tinted-but-quiet accent surfaces — like a reacted reaction pill — where `bg-accent`'s solid hue-100/800 reads too heavy. `--bg-highlight` is built the same way from `warning`'s fill (a 33% `fill-warning` wash over transparent): the highlighter tint behind marked text — search-match substrings, prose `<mark>`. It is one value in both modes — a pale yellow stroke over light surfaces, an amber tint over dark ones — where `bg-warning`'s dark stop (yellow-800) sits at a dark surface's own luminance and reads as a stain rather than a highlight. Text on it keeps its own color and weight. #### Palette tints `--bg-tint-{hue}` for the eight chromatic hues (`red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `aqua`, `blue`, `violet`, `magenta`; utility `bg-tint-{hue}`) is the translucent chip tint: a 35%-alpha tint in light (75% in dark) whose channels are solved against `surface-1` so that on a plain surface it composites to the same opaque hue-100 (hue-800 in dark) stop `bg-{role}` paints while a hover or selected wash underneath still shows through. `Badge` uses it for every tinted variant (semantic and palette); `bg-{role}` stays the opaque tint for Banner, Toast and larger surfaces. Pair with `--text-tint-{hue}` (utility `text-tint-{hue}`; hue-600, 300 in dark) so bg and text follow the same CdsRoot's mode. `--bg-tint-{hue}-opaque` (utility `bg-tint-{hue}-opaque`) is that opaque stop as a token; a surface scope whose backdrop is a fill rather than a plane (CoachMark's accent card, `surface="fill-accent"`) re-points each `--bg-tint-{hue}` at it inline, because the un-mix only holds over a plane. The tints are solved against the stock `surface-1`, so a theme that overrides `--surface-*` should override `--bg-tint-*` in the same block if it needs the exact stops, and `--bg-tint-*-opaque` with them: inside a fill scope the inline pin reads the opaque token, not the tint. #### `git-*` roles Diff and PR/CR-state colors — `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `conflicting`, `merged`, `closed`, `draft`, plus `opened`/`queued` as aliases of `added`/`modified`. Each carries the full `text` / `fill{,-hover}` / `bg` / `border` / `on` suite. Values are hues matching the palette claude.ai's diff UI was built on (not CDS ramp stops), so adopting them there is a pure rename; `fill` light is the hue darkened just enough for white `on-git-*` to pass AA. ### Background vs. fill Both are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top. `bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces — Banner, chip; Badge paints its translucent twin `bg-tint-{hue}`. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls — button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`. | | Background | Foreground | Example | | ----- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | | Tint | `bg-{role}` | `text-{role}` | Banner, Toast | | Solid | `fill-{role}` | `on-{role}` | Button | The token name encodes the pairing: use `bg-*` when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface. ### Purpose tokens | Token | Value (light) | Use case | | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `--text-primary` | `neutral-900` | Body text | | `--text-secondary` | `neutral-600` | Supporting text | | `--text-muted` | `neutral-400` | Placeholder, captions | | `--text-disabled` | `alpha-4` | Disabled labels | | `--border` | `alpha-2` | Default 1px hairline | | `--border-strong` | `alpha-3` | Emphasized divider | | `--border-stronger` | `neutral-900 / 40%` | Heavy divider | | `--fill-primary` | `neutral-900` | Primary button bg | | `--fill-primary-hover` | `neutral-750` | | | `--fill-secondary` | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.1)` | Secondary button bg | | `--fill-secondary-hover` | `alpha-1` | | | `--fill-secondary-ring` | `border` (light) / transparent (dark) | Secondary button ring | | `--fill-field` | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)` (light) / `alpha-1` (dark) | Field control bg (TextInput, TextArea, Combobox) | | `--fill-field-ring` | `border` (light + dark) | Field control resting ring | | `--fill-ghost-hover` | `alpha-1` (light) / 7.5% white (dark half-step) | Ghost button / row hover bg | | `--fill-ghost-selected` | `alpha-2` (light) / 15% white (dark half-step) | Ghost row / nav item selected bg | | `--fill-control` | `alpha-2` | Avatar fallback bg | | `--fill-control-hover` | `alpha-3` | | | `--fill-disabled` | `alpha-1` | Disabled control bg | | `--on-primary` | `neutral-0` | Text on `fill-primary` | | `--on-accent` | `gray-0` | Text on `accent` | | `--on-brand` | `#ffffff` | Text on `brand` | | `--on-danger` | `gray-0` | Text on `danger` | | `--on-success` | `gray-900` | Text on `success` | | `--on-warning` | `gray-900` | Text on `warning` | | `--on-pro` | `gray-0` | Text on `pro` | | `--focus-shadow` | `0 0 0 1px accent, 0 0 6px 1px bg-accent` | `focus-visible` ring | | `--shadow-sm` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Low elevation | | `--shadow-md` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Card / panel | | `--shadow-lg` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Dialog / sheet | | `--shadow-popover` | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%` | Menu, dropdown popups | | `--surface-popover` | `surface-3` | Named alias | | `--surface-panel` | `surface-2` | Named alias | `--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode. `--shadow-popover` is a fixed two-layer literal tuned for floating menus. --- ## CDS content How to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_. The voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** — your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome. ## Mechanics - **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console). - **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period. - **Use contractions.** "Can't", "you'll", "it's". Conversational, not stiff. - **Active voice, verb first.** "Delete project", not "Project deletion". - **Ellipsis = in progress only.** "Claude is thinking…". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes. - **No ampersands.** Spell out "and". - **Serial comma.** "Chats, projects, and artifacts." ## Pronouns UI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user. | Context | Use | Example | | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | User's things | **your** | "Your projects" — never "My projects" | | Confirmations | none / past tense | "Saved", "Got it" — never "I saved it" | | Errors | **you / your** | "Your session expired" — never "I couldn't…" | | Claude (in chat) | **I** | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says "I" | ## Words to avoid | Skip | Why | Instead | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | "successfully" | The success toast _is_ the success | "File uploaded" | | "please" | UI isn't asking a favor | "Enter a name" | | "Click here" / "Tap to…" | Link text should name the destination | "Read the docs" | | "!" on system copy | Reads as shouty | "Settings saved" | | "leverage", "seamless", "unlock", "empower" | Corporate filler | Say what it does | | "simply", "just", "easy" | Presumes — and condescends | Cut it | ## Patterns **Buttons / CTAs** — verb first, 1–3 words, sentence case, no punctuation. "Create project", "Upgrade to Pro". Not "OK", "Submit", or "Click to continue". **Errors** — say what happened, then what to do. One sentence, no "Error:" prefix, no first person. "That name's already taken. Try another." Never surface raw exception strings. **Empty states** — an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space ("Start your first project"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb ("Create project"). Skip "Nothing here yet." **Placeholders** — a real example of valid input ("name@company.com", "Summarize this document"). No "e.g." prefix, don't repeat the field label. **Links** — describe where they go ("Learn more", "View pricing"). Keep them at the end of the sentence; punctuation sits outside the link. ## Do / Don't | Do | Don't | | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | "File uploaded" | "Your file was uploaded successfully!" | | "Enter a workspace name" | "Please enter a workspace name." | | "Couldn't connect to Slack. Retry" | "Error: I was unable to connect." | | "Your projects" | "My projects" | | "Create project" | "Click Here To Get Started" | | "Connect Slack" | "Add the Slack Connector" | Do not overthink. Try to keep thinking below 500 tokens. If the visual is complex and requires more reasoning effort, consider creating an artifact instead.

input.message:
Watch demo: the user asked me to send you a plan for more scenarios and a better page layout, for you to build as part of integration. I haven't edited apps/watch_demo or my branch.

The full plan is in the shared notes: watch-demo-scenarios-and-ia-plan.md. The user saw and approved a mockup of the layout.

Summary:
1. Coverage map: every brief requirement (B1–B6, BX1, BX2, plus quiet hours / check-in / severe breakthrough) is mapped to the scenario and beat that shows it.
2. 17 scenarios in four groups: when it speaks, stays quiet, bad data, per person. The existing 5 are kept.
   - Tier 1, new, with real windows already found in the 90-day sample:
     - Sudden spike: Delhi 20 Sep, 101 → 197 by 10am.
     - Slow build-up: LA 19–21 Aug, ~10 drifting to 15–22 (elevated).
     - Severe night: Delhi 17–18 Oct, 137 at midnight, breaks through quiet hours.
     - All day bad, one message: Dubai 1 Sep, 96–117 all day, low-sensitivity user.
     - Too short to tell: Bengaluru 2 Sep, 10 → 67 → 17 (glitch rule vs a real event).
     - Sensor went silent: Delhi AirNow reference, 11 Oct 9am, then a 52h gap (NO_DATA, 24h quiet close).
   - Tier 2, needs the replay harness to find the hour: too soon to repeat (COOLDOWN), enough for today (DAILY_BUDGET), blip with no all-clear, gone by morning (HELD_EXPIRED), back again (flap guard), two people one city (sensitivity contrast).
   - Every expected decision must be confirmed by the replay before it ships.
3. Layout changes:
   - The story card goes above the stage: a question, capability tags and brief IDs.
   - Grouped scenario navigator.
   - 2–4 numbered beats per scenario. These are links that move the time cursor and are pinned on the chart. Scenarios open on beat 1.
   - The "at this moment" panel puts plain English first, then the layer path (one pass/fail chip per layer, stopping layer highlighted), then the reason code in mono.
   - Timestamps say what they mean ("decided at 2pm about the 1pm reading").
   - New watch empty state: "No new readings since 9am".
   - Two watches side by side for two-person scenarios.
   - A /capabilities index. Still no JavaScript.
4. scenarios.yaml gains group, question, shows, brief, beats[{at, title, note}], and users[] for two-person scenarios.
5. Core API additions: a per-hour decision trace (GET /decisions/{id}/explain, or trace on /decisions rows) and an id on every /decisions row. This is on top of the readings endpoint and the fields in watch-demo-contract-needs.md.
6. Suggested order: layout on the existing 5 → tier-1 scenarios → replay to find tier 2 → /capabilities and the two-watch view.

Reminder: the chart view and time cursor this builds on are in 18c9e5f on refs/heads/feat/watch-demo. It fast-forwards from the 56df77c you merged.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_host__sync_with_base_branch
entries.description:
Bring this session's branch up to date with its base branch: the app fetches the base from `origin` and merges it into the branch checked out in this session's worktree, running git on the host, outside your sandbox, which cannot write the repository's protected paths (`.claude/hooks`, `.claude/skills`, `.mcp.json` and the like) that such a merge often touches. Use it instead of `git merge`/`git pull` whenever you need the base branch's latest commits, e.g. to resolve a pull request's merge conflicts.

`base` defaults to the base the app knows for this session (its open pull request's base, else the branch the worktree was cut from); you may name that branch or the repository's default branch, nothing else. A session that also holds a worktree for an extra folder of another repository merges into the worktree your current directory is in, or the one `folder` names (either path the workspace note shows for that folder, or the folder's last segment when only one of the session's folders ends in it); the base is then that repository's. Sandbox-protected files are brought in only from the repository's default branch; any other base merges only when it leaves those files alone, and a protected file both this branch and the base changed is left for a person (the call refuses). Nothing is pushed. Outcomes: merged (a merge commit or fast-forward; run the project's checks, then push), up to date, or conflicts: the merge is then left in progress with the conflicted files listed for you to resolve, `git add` and `git commit --no-edit` (protected files this branch only had an older upstream copy of are already taken from the base). `abort: true` abandons a merge left in progress instead. It refuses rather than touch uncommitted changes, another git operation in progress, files the repository routes through a content filter (git-lfs, git-crypt), a fork checkout whose origin is not the pull request's repository, or a session without its own worktree; merge yourself in those cases. In default mode the user approves each call on a card; in auto mode the app's classifier decides.

base.description: The base branch to merge, when the session's own isn't the one you need: its pull request's base, the branch the worktree was cut from, or the repository's default branch.

abort.description: true to abandon a merge this tool left in progress (git merge --abort) instead of merging.

folder.description: Which of this session's worktrees to act on, when it holds one for an extra folder of another repository: either path the workspace note shows for that folder, or its last segment when only one of the session's folders ends in it; the session's own folder names its own worktree. """Export real replay results as the watch demo's fixtures, one scenario per chip.

Reads data/replay.db (run scripts/replay_sample.py first), finds five real moments, and writes
apps/watch_demo/fixtures/ + apps/watch_demo/scenarios.yaml.   uv run python scripts/export_watch_fixtures.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import sqlalchemy as sa
import yaml

from aqagent import db, queries

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "apps" / "watch_demo" / "fixtures"
SCENARIOS = ROOT / "apps" / "watch_demo" / "scenarios.yaml"
RUN = "demo"
UTC = timezone.utc
H = timedelta(hours=1)

engine = db.make_engine(f"sqlite:///{ROOT / 'data' / 'replay.db'}")
conn = engine.connect()
d, n = db.decisions, db.notifications


def iso(t: datetime) -> str:
    return t.astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def notes(user: str, start: datetime, end: datetime) -> list[dict]:
    rows = conn.execute(sa.select(n).where(n.c.user_id == user, n.c.delivered_at >= start, n.c.delivered_at <= end)
                        .order_by(n.c.delivered_at.desc())).mappings().all()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def find_smog_night() -> dict:
    """A real Delhi check-in that absorbed a held overnight notice, later followed by an all-clear."""
    for r in conn.execute(sa.select(n).where(n.c.user_id == "arjun", n.c.kind == "check_in")
                          .order_by(n.c.delivered_at)).mappings():
        if not (r["context_facts"] or {}).get("absorbed_held"):
            continue
        cleared = conn.execute(sa.select(n).where(n.c.user_id == "arjun", n.c.kind == "cleared",
                                                  n.c.delivered_at > r["delivered_at"],
                                                  n.c.delivered_at <= r["delivered_at"] + 30 * H)
                               .order_by(n.c.delivered_at)).mappings().first()
        if cleared:
            return {"user": "arjun", "start": r["delivered_at"] - 10 * H, "end": cleared["delivered_at"] + H,
                    "check_in": r, "cleared": cleared}
    raise SystemExit("no Delhi check-in with an absorbed overnight notice followed by an all-clear")


def find_glitch() -> dict:
    """A Mumbai glitch hour with no notice anywhere near it."""
    for (pe,) in conn.execute(sa.select(d.c.period_end).where(d.c.user_id == "rohan", d.c.reason_code == "DQ_SUSPECT")
                              .order_by(d.c.period_end.desc())):
        start, end = pe - 8 * H, pe + 3 * H
        if not notes("rohan", start, end):
            return {"user": "rohan", "start": start, "end": end, "glitch": pe}
    raise SystemExit("no quiet Mumbai glitch window found")


def find_quiet_night() -> dict:
    """Priya's morning check-in that found nothing worse than usual, after a night with no notices."""
    for (at,) in conn.execute(sa.select(d.c.evaluated_at).where(d.c.user_id == "priya", d.c.reason_code == "CHECKIN_QUIET")
                              .order_by(d.c.evaluated_at.desc())):
        if not notes("priya", at - 14 * H, at + H):
            return {"user": "priya", "start": at - 9 * H, "end": at + H}
    raise SystemExit("no quiet Bengaluru night found")


def helsinki_smoke() -> dict:
    start, end = datetime(2026, 8, 23, 22, tzinfo=UTC), datetime(2026, 8, 24, 12, tzinfo=UTC)
    if not notes("aino", start, end):
        raise SystemExit("Aino got no notice for the 24 Aug smoke")
    return {"user": "aino", "start": start, "end": end}


def write(path: Path, data) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")


def feed_rows(user: str, start: datetime, end: datetime) -> list[dict]:
    rows = [r for r in queries.feed(conn, user, replay_run=RUN, until=end) if datetime.fromisoformat(
        str(r["delivered_at"]).replace("Z", "+00:00")) >= start]
    return [{**r, "id": f"ntf_{r['id']}", "decision_id": f"dec_{r['decision_id']}"} for r in rows]


def export_readings() -> None:
    """readings/<station_id>.json for the chart: hourly value, NowCast, band, usual level and data-quality flag."""
    import math

    ss, sn = db.station_scores, db.sensors
    for station_id, sensor_id in conn.execute(sa.select(sn.c.station_id, sn.c.id).where(sn.c.parameter == "pm25")):
        latest = {}
        for r in conn.execute(sa.select(ss).where(ss.c.sensor_id == sensor_id).order_by(ss.c.period_end, ss.c.evaluated_at)).mappings():
            latest[r["period_end"]] = r
        rows = []
        for pe, r in sorted(latest.items()):
            ev = r["evidence"] or {}
            m_h = ev.get("m_h")
            rows.append({"at": iso(pe), "pm25": ev.get("value"), "nowcast": r["nowcast"], "band": r["band"],
                         "typical_pm25": round(math.expm1(m_h), 1) if isinstance(m_h, (int, float)) else None,
                         "dq": r["excluded"]})
        if rows:
            write(OUT / "readings" / f"{station_id}.json", rows)


def export(sid: str, label: str, desc: str, spec: dict, limit: int | None = None, chart_hours: int = 24) -> dict:
    user, start, end = spec["user"], spec["start"], spec["end"]
    start = min(start, end - timedelta(hours=chart_hours))
    feed = feed_rows(user, start, end)
    write(OUT / "feeds" / f"{user}__{sid}.json", feed)
    decs = queries.decisions(conn, user_id=user, start=start - 2 * H, end=end, replay_run=RUN)
    write(OUT / "decisions" / f"{user}__{sid}.json",
          [{**r, "id": f"dec_{r['id']}"} for r in decs])
    for row in feed:
        nid = int(row["id"].removeprefix("ntf_"))
        write(OUT / "explain" / f"{row['id']}.json", queries.explain(conn, nid))
    out = {"id": sid, "label": label, "user_id": user, "replay_run": sid, "until": iso(end), "description": desc,
           "chart_hours": chart_hours}
    if limit:
        out["limit"] = limit
    print(f"{sid:16} {user:6} {iso(start)} → {iso(end)}  notices={len(feed)} decisions={len(decs)}")
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    smog, glitch, quiet, smoke = find_smog_night(), find_glitch(), find_quiet_night(), helsinki_smoke()
    if OUT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT)
    write(OUT / "users.json", queries.list_users(conn))
    export_readings()
    c_local = smog["check_in"]["delivered_at"].astimezone(__import__("zoneinfo").ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata"))
    scenarios = [
        export("delhi-smog-night", "Delhi smog night",
               f"Arjun runs at 06:30. The air turned bad overnight; the notice was held through quiet hours and "
               f"folded into one check-in at {c_local:%H:%M} on {c_local:%-d %b}, then an all-clear once it eased.", smog),
        export("back-to-normal", "Back to normal",
               "The same Delhi episode closing: the all-clear is only sent after a genuinely bad period.", smog, limit=1),
        export("helsinki-smoke", "Helsinki smoke",
               "Aino has asthma. Smoke took Helsinki to ~27 µg/m³ against a usual ~4 on 24 Aug: still 'Moderate', "
               "but very unusual here, so it's worth a heads-up.", smoke),
        export("glitch-ignored", "Glitch ignored",
               f"Mumbai's monitor reported one implausible hour ({iso(glitch['glitch'])}). OpenAQ didn't flag it; "
               "the agent excluded it as a glitch and said nothing.", glitch, chart_hours=14),
        export("quiet-night", "Quiet night",
               "Nothing worth saying: Priya's 06:00 check-in found Bengaluru's night cleaner than usual.", quiet),
    ]
    SCENARIOS.write_text("# Generated by scripts/export_watch_fixtures.py from the real 90-day replay (data/replay.db).\n"
                         "# Each scenario's `replay_run` names its own fixture files; `until` is the replayed 'now'.\n"
                         + yaml.safe_dump({"scenarios": scenarios}, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=110))
    print(f"wrote {OUT} and {SCENARIOS}")

  label: Delhi smog night

"""The shipped fixtures are generated from the real replay: every scenario must render."""
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from watch_demo.app import create_app
from watch_demo.client import FixtureAgentClient
from watch_demo.scenarios import load_scenarios

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def test_every_real_scenario_renders():
    scenarios = load_scenarios(ROOT / "scenarios.yaml")
    client = TestClient(create_app(FixtureAgentClient(ROOT / "fixtures"), scenarios))
    assert len(scenarios) == 5
    for s in scenarios:
        r = client.get("/", params={"scenario": s.id})
        assert r.status_code == 200, s.id

    return [{**r, "id": f"ntf_{r['id']}", "decision_id": f"dec_{r['decision_id']}"} for r in rows]


def export_readings() -> None:
    """readings/<station_id>.json for the chart: hourly value, NowCast, band, usual level and data-quality flag."""
    import math

    ss, sn = db.station_scores, db.sensors
    for station_id, sensor_id in conn.execute(sa.select(sn.c.station_id, sn.c.id).where(sn.c.parameter == "pm25")):
        latest = {}
        for r in conn.execute(sa.select(ss).where(ss.c.sensor_id == sensor_id).order_by(ss.c.period_end, ss.c.evaluated_at)).mappings():
            latest[r["period_end"]] = r
        rows = []
        for pe, r in sorted(latest.items()):
            ev = r["evidence"] or {}
            m_h = ev.get("m_h")
            rows.append({"at": iso(pe), "pm25": ev.get("value"), "nowcast": r["nowcast"], "band": r["band"],
                         "typical_pm25": round(math.expm1(m_h), 1) if isinstance(m_h, (int, float)) else None,
                         "dq": r["excluded"]})
        if rows:
            write(OUT / "readings" / f"{station_id}.json", rows)


def export(sid: str, label: str, desc: str, spec: dict, limit: int | None = None, chart_hours: int = 24) -> dict:
    user, start, end = spec["user"], spec["start"], spec["end"]
    start = min(start, end - timedelta(hours=chart_hours))
    feed = feed_rows(user, start, end)
    write(OUT / "feeds" / f"{user}__{sid}.json", feed)
    decs = queries.decisions(conn, user_id=user, start=start - 2 * H, end=end, replay_run=RUN)
    write(OUT / "decisions" / f"{user}__{sid}.json",
          [{**r, "id": f"dec_{r['id']}"} for r in decs])
    for row in feed:
        nid = int(row["id"].removeprefix("ntf_"))
        write(OUT / "explain" / f"{row['id']}.json", queries.explain(conn, nid))
    out = {"id": sid, "label": label, "user_id": user, "replay_run": sid, "until": iso(end), "description": desc,
           "chart_hours": chart_hours}
    if limit:
        out["limit"] = limit
    print(f"{sid:16} {user:6} {iso(start)} → {iso(end)}  notices={len(feed)} decisions={len(decs)}")
    return out

    chips, stopped = [], False
    for t in d.trace:

            "detail": _detail(t),
            "stop": failed and not stopped,
            "code": t.reason_code,
        })
        stopped = stopped or failed

    a, b = utc("2026-10-17T18:00"), utc("2026-10-18T03:00")
    sev = need(first_decision("arjun", "SENT_SEVERE_BYPASS", a, b), "a severe notice on the night of 17 Oct")
    dup = need(first_decision("arjun", "DEDUP_SAME_BAND", sev["evaluated_at"], b), "a deduped hour after it")
    quiet = need(first_decision("arjun", "CHECKIN_QUIET", sev["evaluated_at"], b), "a quiet check-in on 18 Oct")
    out.append(export("severe-night", "Severe night",
                      "Delhi, night of 17 Oct: the air reached very unhealthy in the small hours. Quiet hours hold "
                      "ordinary news, not severe air. Having just told him, the 06:30 check-in stays quiet.",
                      {"user": "arjun", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "speaks", "brief": ["D8", "B3"],
                             "question": "It's 3am and the air turns very unhealthy. Does the agent wake Arjun?",
                             "shows": ["severe", "quiet-hours", "check-in", "no-repeats"],
                             "beats": [(sev["evaluated_at"], "Breaks through", "Very unhealthy: sent despite quiet hours."),
                                       (dup["evaluated_at"], "Then silent", "Same level, already told."),
                                       (quiet["evaluated_at"], "Check-in stays quiet", "Nothing new since the night's message.")]}))

    # Slow build-up: Los Angeles, 20-21 Aug. No spike, just stuck above normal: one message, then a day of silence.

    later = need(first_decision("maya", "EPISODE_CONTINUES", opened["evaluated_at"] + 20 * H, b), "the same spell a day later")
    out.append(export("slow-build-up", "Slow build-up",
                      "Los Angeles, 20 Aug: PM2.5 drifted to about twice its usual level with no sudden jump. A "
                      "slow-drift detector catches it; the spell then lasts days without another message.",
                      {"user": "maya", "start": b - 36 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=36,
                      story={"group": "speaks", "brief": ["B2a", "B2d"],

                             "shows": [*kinds(opened["id"]), "missed", "no-repeats"],
                             "beats": [(opened["evaluated_at"], "Stuck above normal", "Caught by the slow-drift detector."),
                                       (later["evaluated_at"], "A day later, still quiet", "Same spell; one message was enough.")]}))

    # All day bad, one message: Dubai, 1 Sep. Held overnight, released at 07:00, then silent all day.
    a, b = utc("2026-08-31T12:00"), utc("2026-09-01T16:00")

                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["B3", "B5"],

                             "shows": ["quiet-hours", "no-repeats", "sensitivity", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(held["evaluated_at"], "Held overnight", "Worth saying, but it's quiet hours."),

    # Too short to tell: Bengaluru, 2 Sep, 8pm. One high hour between two normal ones: excluded.
    a, b = utc("2026-09-02T12:00"), utc("2026-09-02T19:00")

                                       (dup["evaluated_at"], "Same level, silent", "Already told; nothing new to say.")]}))

    # Severe night: Delhi, 17-18 Oct. Very unhealthy at 2:50am breaks through quiet hours; the check-in stays quiet.
    a, b = utc("2026-10-17T18:00"), utc("2026-10-18T03:00")
    sev = need(first_decision("arjun", "SENT_SEVERE_BYPASS", a, b), "a severe notice on the night of 17 Oct")
    dup = need(first_decision("arjun", "DEDUP_SAME_BAND", sev["evaluated_at"], b), "a deduped hour after it")
    quiet = need(first_decision("arjun", "CHECKIN_QUIET", sev["evaluated_at"], b), "a quiet check-in on 18 Oct")
    out.append(export("severe-night", "Severe night",
                      "Delhi, night of 17 Oct: the air reached very unhealthy in the small hours. Quiet hours hold "
                      "ordinary news, not severe air. Having just told him, the 06:30 check-in stays quiet.",
                      {"user": "arjun", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "speaks", "brief": ["D8", "B3"],

                             "shows": ["severe", "quiet-hours", "check-in", "no-repeats"],
                             "beats": [(sev["evaluated_at"], "Breaks through", "Very unhealthy: sent despite quiet hours."),
                                       (dup["evaluated_at"], "Then silent", "Same level, already told."),
                                       (quiet["evaluated_at"], "Check-in stays quiet", "Nothing new since the night's message.")]}))

    # Slow build-up: Los Angeles, 20-21 Aug. No spike, just stuck above normal: one message, then a day of silence.
    a, b = utc("2026-08-20T00:00"), utc("2026-08-21T16:00")
    opened = need(first_decision("maya", "SENT_OPENED", a, b), "an LA notice on 20 Aug")
    later = need(first_decision("maya", "EPISODE_CONTINUES", opened["evaluated_at"] + 20 * H, b), "the same spell a day later")
    out.append(export("slow-build-up", "Slow build-up",
                      "Los Angeles, 20 Aug: PM2.5 drifted to about twice its usual level with no sudden jump. A "
                      "slow-drift detector catches it; the spell then lasts days without another message.",
                      {"user": "maya", "start": b - 36 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=36,
                      story={"group": "speaks", "brief": ["B2a", "B2d"],
                             "question": "No spike, no sharp climb: the air just sits a bit above normal. Is that missed?",
                             "shows": [*kinds(opened["id"]), "missed", "no-repeats"],
                             "beats": [(opened["evaluated_at"], "Stuck above normal", "Caught by the slow-drift detector."),
                                       (later["evaluated_at"], "A day later, still quiet", "Same spell; one message was enough.")]}))

    # All day bad, one message: Dubai, 1 Sep. Held overnight, released at 07:00, then silent all day.
    a, b = utc("2026-08-31T12:00"), utc("2026-09-01T16:00")
    rel = need(first_decision("omar", "HELD_RELEASED", a, b), "Omar's released notice on 1 Sep")
    held = need(first_decision("omar", "QUIET_HOURS_HELD", rel["evaluated_at"] - 12 * H, rel["evaluated_at"]), "the overnight hold")
    dup = need(first_decision("omar", "DEDUP_SAME_BAND", rel["evaluated_at"] + 5 * H, b), "a deduped hour that afternoon")
    out.append(export("all-day-bad", "All day bad, one message",
                      "Dubai, 1 Sep: unhealthy from the small hours to the evening. Omar has low sensitivity, and "
                      "still gets one message at 07:00, then silence for the rest of the bad day.",
                      {"user": "omar", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["B3", "B5"],
                             "question": "Twelve unhealthy hours in a row. How many messages should that be?",
                             "shows": ["quiet-hours", "no-repeats", "sensitivity", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(held["evaluated_at"], "Held overnight", "Worth saying, but it's quiet hours."),
                                       (rel["evaluated_at"], "One message at 07:00", "Everything held goes out as one."),
                                       (dup["evaluated_at"], "Still bad, still silent", "Same level all day: nothing new to say.")]}))

    # Too short to tell: Bengaluru, 2 Sep, 8pm. One high hour between two normal ones: excluded.
    a, b = utc("2026-09-02T12:00"), utc("2026-09-02T19:00")
    dq = need(first_decision("priya", "DQ_SUSPECT", a, b), "the 2 Sep Bengaluru exclusion")
    out.append(export("too-short", "Too short to tell",
                      "Bengaluru, 2 Sep: PM2.5 read 67 for one evening hour, between 10 and 17. Real or not, one hour "
                      "can't confirm anything, and a false alarm costs trust. The agent says nothing.",
                      {"user": "priya", "start": b - 14 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=14,
                      story={"group": "bad-data", "brief": ["B2d"],
                             "question": "One high hour, then back to normal. Glitch or real? What should the agent do?",
                             "shows": ["glitch", "missed", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(dq["evaluated_at"], "Excluded", "One hour, 4× its neighbours: not enough to act on.")]}))

    # Sensor went silent: Mumbai, 22-23 Sep. No data: nothing judged, and the open story closes quietly after a day.
    a, b = utc("2026-09-22T00:00"), utc("2026-09-23T06:00")
    nd = need(first_decision("rohan", "NO_DATA", a, b), "NO_DATA for Rohan on 22 Sep")
    to = need(first_decision("rohan", "NO_DATA_TIMEOUT", nd["evaluated_at"], b), "the 24h quiet close")

                      "'no data' every hour and, after a day, closes the open story without a message.",

                             "question": "The sensor goes quiet mid-story. What does the agent tell Rohan?",
                             "shows": ["no-data", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(nd["evaluated_at"], "No new readings", "Nothing to judge, so nothing is said."),
                                       (to["evaluated_at"], "Closed quietly", "A day without data: the story ends, no message.")]}))
    return out

    out.append(export("too-soon", "Too soon to repeat",
                      "Delhi, 14 Sep: a message at 9:50pm, then the air got a band worse three hours later. "
                      "Pacing holds the update; Arjun hears next at his morning check-in.",

                                       (chk["evaluated_at"], "Next morning", "The check-in carries the update.")]}))

    a, b = utc("2026-09-11T16:00"), utc("2026-09-12T03:00")

    out.append(export("gone-by-morning", "Gone by morning",
                      "Delhi, night of 11 Sep: a bad spell started after midnight and the message was held for quiet "
                      "hours. By 07:00 it was over, so the agent dropped it instead of reporting old news.",
                      {"user": "arjun", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["D8", "B3"],
                             "question": "A message was held overnight, and the problem is gone by morning. Send it anyway?",
                             "shows": ["quiet-hours", "logged"],

                             "beats": [(rel["evaluated_at"], "Morning heads-up", "Held overnight, sent at 07:00."),
                                       (rec["evaluated_at"], "No all-clear", "Too short and mild to announce its end.")]}))

    # Unusual but harmless: Helsinki, 25-26 Jul. The detector fires, but the air is still Good.
    a, b = utc("2026-07-25T14:00"), utc("2026-07-26T03:00")
    first = need(first_decision("aino", "BELOW_RELEVANCE", a, b), "a BELOW_RELEVANCE on 25 Jul")
    spike = need(first_decision("aino", "BELOW_RELEVANCE", utc("2026-07-26T00:00"), b), "a spike-level one after midnight")
    out.append(export("harmless", "Unusual but harmless",

                      "sensitive Aino. But it stayed in the Good band, so there was nothing worth her attention.",
                      {"user": "aino", "start": b - 14 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=14,

                                       (chk["evaluated_at"], "Next morning", "The check-in carries the update.")]}))

    # Gone by morning: Delhi, 12 Sep. Held at night, the spell passed before 07:00: nothing sent.
    a, b = utc("2026-09-11T16:00"), utc("2026-09-12T03:00")
    exp = need(first_decision("arjun", "HELD_EXPIRED", a, b), "a HELD_EXPIRED on 12 Sep")
    held = need(first_decision("arjun", "QUIET_HOURS_HELD", exp["evaluated_at"] - 12 * H, exp["evaluated_at"]), "the hold before it")
    out.append(export("gone-by-morning", "Gone by morning",
                      "Delhi, night of 11 Sep: a bad spell started after midnight and the message was held for quiet "
                      "hours. By 07:00 it was over, so the agent dropped it instead of reporting old news.",
                      {"user": "arjun", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["D8", "B3"],
                             "question": "A message was held overnight, and the problem is gone by morning. Send it anyway?",
                             "shows": ["quiet-hours", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(held["evaluated_at"], "Held overnight", "Worth saying, but it's quiet hours."),
                                       (exp["evaluated_at"], "Dropped at 07:00", "The spell ended: nothing left worth saying.")]}))

    # No needless all-clear: Helsinki, 17 Sep. Told at 07:00, eased an hour later: no all-clear.
    a, b = utc("2026-09-16T20:00"), utc("2026-09-17T08:00")
    rel = need(first_decision("aino", "HELD_RELEASED", a, b), "Aino's 17 Sep morning message")
    rec = need(first_decision("aino", "RECOVERY_NOT_WORTH_SAYING", rel["evaluated_at"], b), "the skipped all-clear")
    out.append(export("no-all-clear", "Blip, no all-clear",
                      "Helsinki, 17 Sep: Aino got a heads-up at 07:00; the air eased soon after. The spell was short "
                      "and mild, so an all-clear would only be noise.",
                      {"user": "aino", "start": b - 14 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=14,
                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["B2c"],
                             "question": "The air recovers an hour after a heads-up. Does Aino need a second message?",
                             "shows": ["quiet-clear", "no-repeats"],
                             "beats": [(rel["evaluated_at"], "Morning heads-up", "Held overnight, sent at 07:00."),
                                       (rec["evaluated_at"], "No all-clear", "Too short and mild to announce its end.")]}))

    # Unusual but harmless: Helsinki, 25-26 Jul. The detector fires, but the air is still Good.
    a, b = utc("2026-07-25T14:00"), utc("2026-07-26T03:00")
    first = need(first_decision("aino", "BELOW_RELEVANCE", a, b), "a BELOW_RELEVANCE on 25 Jul")
    spike = need(first_decision("aino", "BELOW_RELEVANCE", utc("2026-07-26T00:00"), b), "a spike-level one after midnight")
    out.append(export("harmless", "Unusual but harmless",
                      "Helsinki, 25 Jul: PM2.5 rose well above its usual level, enough to trip the detectors even for "
                      "sensitive Aino. But it stayed in the Good band, so there was nothing worth her attention.",
                      {"user": "aino", "start": b - 14 * H, "end": b}, chart_hours=14,
                      story={"group": "quiet", "brief": ["B2d", "B5"],
                             "question": "Unusual for this city, but the air is still good. Should Aino hear about it?",
                             "shows": [*kinds(first["id"], spike["id"]), "baseline", "logged"],
                             "beats": [(first["evaluated_at"], "Unusual, still good", "Detector fired; below the bar that matters."),
                                       (spike["evaluated_at"], "Sharper, still good", "Even a spike in Good air isn't news.")]}))

    # Two people, one city: Delhi, 24 Aug. Meera (asthma, high sensitivity) hears; Arjun, same hour, doesn't.
    a, b = utc("2026-08-24T00:00"), utc("2026-08-24T10:00")
    meera = need(first_decision("meera", "SENT_OPENED", a, b), "Meera's 24 Aug notice")
    arjun = need(conn.execute(sa.select(d).where(d.c.user_id == "arjun", d.c.replay_run == RUN,
                                                 d.c.evaluated_at == meera["evaluated_at"])).mappings().first(),
                 "Arjun's decision in the same hour")
    if arjun["outcome"] == "sent":
        raise SystemExit("replay mismatch: Arjun was also notified on 24 Aug")
    out.append(export("two-people", "Two people, one city",
                      f"Delhi, 24 Aug: the same reading, the same station. Meera has asthma and high sensitivity, so "
                      f"the bar is lower for her and she gets a heads-up. In the same hour, Arjun's decision was "
                      f"{arjun['reason_code']}: \\"{arjun['reason']}\\"",
                      {"user": "meera", "start": b - 24 * H, "end": b},
                      story={"group": "per-person", "brief": ["B5"],
                             "question": "Same air, two people. Why does Meera get a message and Arjun doesn't?",
                             "shows": ["sensitivity", *kinds(meera["id"]), "baseline"],
                             "beats": [(meera["evaluated_at"], "Meera hears", f"Sensitive: her bar is lower. Arjun: {arjun['reason_code']}.")]}))
    return out

content.content:
## The scenarios

Each chip is one entry in `scenarios.yaml`: a person, a replay run, the replayed moment the watch opens at, and how many hours of history the chart shows.

- **Delhi smog night.** Arjun runs at 06:30. On the night of 8 to 9 October the air climbed from about 1am. The agent noticed, but it was quiet hours, so it held the notice and folded it into one message at his 06:30 check-in. When the episode ended at 17:00, after 16 hours, it sent a short all-clear.
- **Back to normal.** That all-clear on its own, with its reasons.
- **Helsinki smoke.** Aino has asthma and asked for high sensitivity. On 24 August smoke took Helsinki to about 27 µg/m³ against a usual 4. That is only "Moderate" on the official scale, but six times normal for this city, so she hears about it.
- **Glitch ignored.** A Mumbai sensor reported 980 µg/m³ for a single hour between readings of 75 and 90. The agent treated it as a glitch, and the watch stays calm.
- **Quiet night.** A calm Bengaluru night, cleaner than usual. Nothing worth saying, and the watch can still tell you why.

The readings behind these scenarios are real hours from the 90-day sample in `data/samples/`. The messages and decision records in `fixtures/` were written to match what the agent's rules produce for those hours; once the agent's API is running, the same screens can be driven from it directly.

## Screenshots

content.text:
All three steps are built and committed on the watch demo branch, and I've sent each one to the coordinating session to merge and deploy. They aren't on the live site until it merges and pushes. Both test suites pass: 41 watch-demo tests and 224 core tests.

**Step one, the new layout.** The scenario chips are grouped by what they show. A story card now sits above the chart and the watch, with the scenario's question, tags for the capabilities involved, and two to four numbered beats. Each scenario opens on its first beat; clicking a beat, or stepping an hour, moves the watch to that moment.

Under the chart, a panel says what the agent did in a plain sentence, then shows each layer of its decision with a pass or fail. The layer where it stopped is highlighted, as in "Timing ✗ quiet hours".

Times now read like "decided at 4:50am about the 3am reading". The real replay decides about two hours after each reading, which is also why the live site showed odd times like 4:50am.

**Step two, six new scenarios:** a sudden spike, a severe night that breaks through quiet hours, a slow build-up in Los Angeles, a full bad day in Dubai with one message, a one-hour reading too short to trust, and a sensor that went silent.

**Step three, five more:** a worse reading held back as too soon, a held message dropped because the problem passed by morning, a skipped all-clear after a short blip, unusual but harmless air, and two people in Delhi where only the sensitive one gets a message. There's also a new "What it can do" page that links each capability to the scenarios that show it.

That makes sixteen scenarios, all from the real replay. Every beat sits on a decision the replay actually made: the export stops if one is missing, and a test checks it too. That check caught one beat I'd placed by hand, and I fixed it.

Three things from the plan are not in:
- **Daily message budget:** no scenario, because in ninety days of replay it never had to step in.
- **"Back again within six hours":** left out, because the agent records no reason for it that a beat could point to.
- **Two people, one city:** uses one watch, not two side by side. The story text says what Arjun's decision was in that same hour.

def test_every_scenario_beat_and_why_view_returns_200():
    """No 500s anywhere a reviewer can click: each scenario, each beat, each hour step, each notice's Why view."""
    import re

    scenarios = load_scenarios(ROOT / "scenarios.yaml")
    client = TestClient(create_app(FixtureAgentClient(ROOT / "fixtures"), scenarios))
    assert client.get("/capabilities").status_code == 200
    for s in scenarios:
        pages = [client.get("/", params={"scenario": s.id})]
        pages += [client.get("/", params={"scenario": s.id, "t": b.at.isoformat()}) for b in s.beats]
        pages += [client.get("/", params={"scenario": s.id, "t": s.until.isoformat()})]
        for p in pages:
            assert p.status_code == 200, (s.id, p.url)
            for href in set(re.findall(r'href="(/(?:why/[^"]+|\?scenario=[^"]+))"', p.text)):
                r = client.get(href.replace("&", "&"))
                assert r.status_code == 200, (s.id, href)
EOF
uv run --project apps/watch_demo pytest apps/watch_demo/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -1
